chunks: What Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
He said: O Zurārah, you begin the adhān with four takbīrs, and you conclude it with two takbīrs and two tahlīls.

key_terms.أَرْبَعِ: four, indicating the number of opening takbīrs
key_terms.تَهْلِيلَتَيْنِ: two declarations of 'Lā ilāha illā Allāh'

ai.seo_question: How many takbīrs and tahlīls are recited in the adhān according to Imam al-Bāqir عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states the prescribed number of certain phrases in the adhān. It instructs that the adhān begins with four takbīrs and ends with two takbīrs and two declarations of tahlīl, indicating a legal ruling related to the form of ritual worship.
